package_info.why_malicious: These packages are brandjacking/typosquatting attacks that impersonate legitimate Maven and Jenkins plugins. Each contains backdoored code that downloads and executes arbitrary code from attacker-controlled servers, enabling remote code execution, system compromise, and persistent access. The malicious payloads are triggered during normal plugin operations, targeting developer machines and CI/CD build servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime during plugin execution, the code downloads a remote JAR from a hardcoded C2 server, dynamically loads it into the JVM using reflection, and executes a class from it, resulting in arbitrary code execution from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a JAR from an untrusted, hardcoded remote server using reflection and dynamic class loading, which is a classic remote code execution backdoor technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Maven plugins should not download or execute code from external sources at runtime; they are expected to operate only on local project files and dependencies resolved from trusted repositories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin loading from trusted, signed repositories (never from arbitrary URLs or untrusted sources).
key_indicators: Hardcoded external URL (C2 server) in code
Use of reflection to invoke addURL on URLClassLoader
Dynamic class loading and execution of remote code
No user interaction or consent required
Runs as part of normal Maven build process

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On mail notification event, the code downloads a Groovy script from a hardcoded C2 server, writes it to disk at /tmp/evil.groovy, and evaluates it in a GroovyShell, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the Jenkins server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fetches and executes a Groovy script from an untrusted remote server, directly enabling arbitrary code execution via GroovyShell evaluation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate notification plugins should only send notifications and must not download or execute remote scripts or code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated script updates from trusted, signed sources (rare in plugins, and never via direct GroovyShell evaluation of remote code).
key_indicators: Hardcoded external URL (C2 server) for script download
No user interaction or consent required
Executes on mail notification event in Jenkins

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request to web application)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every HTTP GET request, the code executes a base64-decoded reverse shell command using bash, which connects to the attacker's server and grants remote shell access to the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a base64-encoded reverse shell command that connects to a hardcoded external IP and port, providing attackers with direct command-line access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate servlet APIs should never execute shell commands or open reverse shells in response to HTTP requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; reverse shells and arbitrary shell command execution are never legitimate in servlet APIs.
key_indicators: Base64-encoded shell command embedded in servlet code
Reverse shell connection to external IP and port
Shell command execution on every HTTP GET request
No authentication or user interaction required

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed or used as a dependency in a developer's project or CI/CD pipeline.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed during normal plugin or application operation.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code triggers on plugin execution, mail notification, or HTTP request, depending on the component.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code or script is downloaded and executed from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution or shell access on the victim machine (developer workstation, CI server, or web server).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can exfiltrate data, move laterally, or persist on the compromised system.

behavioral_signatures: Plugin or library code that downloads and executes code from external URLs at runtime
Use of reflection to invoke addURL on URLClassLoader for dynamic class loading
GroovyShell evaluation of remote scripts downloaded from external sources
Base64-decoded and executed shell commands in servlet or plugin code
Reverse shell connections initiated by web applications or build plugins
file_indicators: Unusual modifications to plugin JARs (CompilerMojo.class, MailWatcherNotification.class, HttpServlet.class)
Unexpected network or process execution code in plugin or servlet classes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Java plugin and servlet code for hardcoded external URLs, use of reflection for dynamic class loading, GroovyShell evaluation of remote scripts, and base64-decoded shell commands. Monitor for network connections to known C2 domains/IPs. Alert on plugins or servlets that write to /tmp/evil.groovy or execute shell commands. Use static analysis to flag code that downloads and executes remote code or scripts, and dynamic analysis to detect reverse shell activity.
